accuracy.evidence: Matches Y1 Science plants: name wild/garden plants; deciduous lose leaves; evergreen keep leaves; daisy/grass/rose/oak/holly examples from NC plant list.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets every-tree-loses-leaves, holly-as-deciduous, grass-not-a-plant, and name mix-ups in sort, match, keep, challenge why(), and adult notes.

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab is naming and deciduous/evergreen sorting — distinct from plant parts (flagplant), seed growth (flagseed), and water/light needs (flagsprout).

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner names daisy, sorts lose/keep leaves, sorts wild/garden, matches holly clue, picks evergreen, then reads confirming text.

predictions.evidence: Wrong options (oak=daisy, every tree loses leaves, rose=wild oak, grass not plant) are overturned by name/decid/wild/keep tasks.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() names metal/oak/daisy, keep/lose/bareoak, never/dead/noplant, wildoak/talltree slips specifically.

readability.evidence: Ages 5–6 wording: short kid lines; deciduous/evergreen introduced with lose/keep leaves.

no_filler.evidence: No delve/journey phrasing; each line teaches naming, leaf habit, or wild vs garden.

mobile.evidence: Large name/sort buttons; tap twins for drag; challenge stack usable at phone width; young class.

accessibility.evidence: Name, decid, wild, match, idea, keep expose lbtn twins; say() updates canvas aria-label; challenge uses aria-live status.

sources: UK National Curriculum Science Y1: identify and name a variety of common wild and garden plants, including deciduous and evergreen trees
BBC Bitesize KS1 Science: plants — common plants; evergreen and deciduous trees
RHS / Woodland Trust education: oak deciduous; holly evergreen
